frozenCoreClassification: P0-P9 kernel, proof, policy, constitution, and ledger modules plus their migrations and the canonical closure/Cedar verification scripts. These implement the admission decision, proof storage, and provenance invariants that the two closure missions adversarially verified. Modifying any of these requires a reproduced operational defect, not integration convenience — see the amendment protocol below.
digestAlgorithm: sha256 over raw file bytes as committed at canonicalClosureTestedSha, computed with node:crypto createHash('sha256')

explicitlyNotFrozen.src/omnia-v9/outbound-shadow.mjs: pre-existing P0-level shadow adapter, designed to be extended for integration
explicitlyNotFrozen.src/omnia-v9/final-admission-shadow.mjs: pre-existing P4-level shadow adapter and the exact seam this integration extends; classified as integration glue, not kernel
explicitlyNotFrozen.src/omnia-v9/integrations/**: new in this mission; this is the integration layer itself, expected to evolve independently of the frozen core

knownLimitations: PostgreSQL used for closure verification is a native local install, not the Docker postgres:16 image CI uses (same major version and pgcrypto extension)
Mutation testing across both closure passes covers ten named critical protections; it is not an exhaustive sweep of every conceivable mutation
Browser test suite (tests/browser.test.mjs) cannot run in the verification sandbox due to a pre-existing Playwright browser-revision mismatch unrelated to V9

No real Cedar-backed policy or owner-issued approval exists in production yet; V9's admission decisions in this integration will be evidence-limited until real approvals are issued (see V9_REAL_INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md)
architecturalFreezeStatement: As of this baseline, OMNIA V9's P0-P9 core (admission kernel, proof store, constitution/policy binding, Cedar evaluation, execution-receipt and authorization-binding stores, and the authority-transition ledger) is frozen. No new constitutional abstractions, governance layers, or architectural expansion may be added to this core without: (1) a reproduced real operational defect, (2) measured evidence of the failure, (3) an explicit statement of which invariant changes, and (4) a new regression test proving the fix and guarding against regression. This baseline exists precisely so that future changes are judged against it rather than against vague architectural ambition.
